questions.prompt: An object starts from rest and accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. What is its final velocity?
A scooter at 10 m/s accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s. How far does it travel?
A car at 20 m/s decelerates at 5 m/s² to rest. How far does it travel while braking?
A stone is dropped from a 45 m cliff (take g = 10 m/s², ignore air). How long does it take to reach the ground?
questions.explain: 45 = ½ × 10 × t², so t² = 9 and t = 3 s.

questions.prompt: A car moving at 25 m/s brakes at 5 m/s². What is its braking distance?
If a car's speed is doubled, what happens to its braking distance (same braking force)?
options: It becomes four times as long
questions.explain: s = u² ÷ 2a, so s depends on the square of the speed.

questions.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up at 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). How high does it rise?
questions.explain: At the top v = 0: 0 = 400 − 20s, so s = 20 m.

questions.prompt: Using the equations of motion, explain why using a phone while driving is so dangerous, even for a second or two.
questions.modelAnswer: During reaction time, the car keeps moving at full speed before the driver even starts braking. At 20 m/s, 2 extra seconds of distraction adds 40 m of travel (s = vt). Then the braking distance (s = u²/2a) is added on top. Together this total stopping distance can be longer than the distance to a hazard, so the driver can't stop in time.
questions.explain: Criterion D: impact of science on everyday decisions.
